walkthroughs.body_html:
Independent Investigation (NEA) — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Independent Investigation (NEA) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Independent Investigation (NEA).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Why might managed retreat be more sustainable than building a sea wall?
options: Sea walls are expensive, deflect erosion elsewhere and reflect wave energy worsening beach loss; managed retreat works with natural processes, creates habitat and is cheaper long-term.
Tsunamis are caused by the moon's gravity at full moon.
Managed retreat means letting all coastal towns disappear into the sea.
Sea walls always solve coastal erosion problems permanently.

mcqs.q: Why do some rivers form deltas and others form estuaries?
options: Deltas form on big rivers and estuaries on small ones.
Deltas form in cold climates and estuaries in warm climates.
Managed retreat means letting all coastal towns disappear into the sea.
Deltas form where rivers deposit sediment faster than the sea can remove it (calm seas, heavy load); estuaries form where tidal energy removes sediment (strong tides).
The sudden vertical displacement of a large volume of water, usually by an undersea earthquake, but also by underwater landslides or volcanic eruptions.
